## Summary

Her recipe for creating a `claude.md` is not hand-writing rules — it's **delegating the digest of a curated corpus**. She had Claude read:

- her favorite programming books + blogs,
- the best OSS projects,
- the code of the engineers she respects the most.

The result, her claim: "Claude (when given proper instructions, constraints, and context) now writes better code than me, almost always." The tweet is a reply into the "coding agent haters getting Dunning-Kruger'd" discourse — her "almost always" is the measured version of the quoted take that the model already beats most engineers.

## Why it matters

- **The mechanism is taste transfer by exemplar, not by rule.** A hand-written CLAUDE.md can *say* "write clean, idiomatic code"; a corpus of the books, blogs, OSS and engineers the author already trusts *shows* what she means by good. The model infers the standard from examples — the same way it learned code in the first place. She's running a personal preference-tuning pass at the context layer.
- **This names a third stratum for the instructions-file model.** [[2026-10-01-mikeysee-claude-md-what-i-need]] is the transient stratum ("What I need from you", rewritten each session); [[2026-09-26-pocock-coding-standards-accretion]] is the slow stratum (standards accreted from failures). Sridharan's is the **taste stratum**: distilled once from exemplars the author vouches for, changed only when the corpus changes. Three layers, three lifecycles, same file.
- **The flip side is her own debugging note.** A week ago she documented that fixing a bug in ~9K LOC of AI-generated code defeated every classic tactic ([[2026-10-11-copyconstruct-debugging-agents-unreadable-code]]). Together the two tweets are the full bargain: the output can now beat your best day, *and* you no longer hold the mental model needed to fix it when it breaks. Better-than-me code and unreadable-code are the same coin.
- **Curation is the hidden skill — and it's circular.** The file inherits the quality of what got included: books/blogs/OSS/engineers *she* already judged best. You need taste to build the taste file. That makes the method an amplifier of existing judgment, not a substitute for it — which is also why it plausibly works for her (deep, decades-built filter) and may disappoint when copied by someone borrowing others' "best-of" lists.
- **Direct relevance to us.** Our agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md) are built almost entirely the Pocock way — rules accreted from failures. A complementary one-time play: curate our own exemplar corpus (the engineering blogs/OSS/reference repos we already consider best-in-class) and have a model distill a taste section from it, then judge the output delta on a real task.
- **Skepticism gates:** (1) n=1 self-report — "better code than me, almost always" with no tasks, baselines, or before/after; (2) survivorship — we see the winning config, not the corpus attempts that didn't move the needle; (3) cost is unmeasured — having Claude read "the best OSS projects" is a large context/compute spend per refresh; (4) "fable" in the quoted tweet is an unverified model reference from a partisan frame; (5) quoted text truncated at capture, so the strongest claim in the chain is only half-visible.

- **Isolation note (CoS convention):** personal second-brain knowledge capture only; nothing routed to the trading company.
